title: Nine bullets hit him in the 1965 war. He still won India's first Paralympic gold. October 16, 2026.
excerpt: From a satellite that freed India from borrowed navigation systems, to a Harvard professor honored as a great American immigrant, to a Fortune 500 CEO funding a scholarship named after her mother - today's stories are about building the thing yourself instead of depending on someone else for it.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about replacing dependence with self-sufficiency - a navigation system no longer borrowed from another country, a semiconductor industry no longer entirely imported, a body that stopped depending on legs it no longer had, careers built not on someone else's institutions but inside the world's best ones, and a gift designed to make sure the next woman in an engineering class isn't the only one.

October 16, 2014: India launched the third satellite of a navigation system it was building entirely on its own

ISRO launched IRNSS-1C aboard a PSLV-C26 rocket from Sriharikota - the third of seven satellites in what would become NavIC, India's own satellite navigation system, independent of foreign GPS networks.

He's spent more than four decades teaching at Harvard Medical School. Carnegie just named him one of America's great immigrants

Dr. Sanjiv Chopra, a Harvard Medical School professor who moved to the US in 1972 for residency training, was named to Carnegie Corporation's 2026 Great Immigrants, Great Americans list.

A Fortune 500 CEO just funded a scholarship named after her mother

Revathi Advaithi, CEO of Flex and a BITS Pilani alumna, and her husband Jeevan Mulgund endowed a $1 million permanent scholarship fund for women from economically weaker backgrounds, announced at BITS Pilani's July 2026 convocation and named after both their mothers.

India's Cabinet just approved its last two semiconductor plants - and the program is now complete

The Union Cabinet approved two final semiconductor units in Gujarat, completing the India Semiconductor Mission's first phase: 12 approved projects across five states, with cumulative investment near Rs 1.64 lakh crore.

Nine bullets hit him in the 1965 war. He still won India's first Paralympic gold

Murlikant Petkar was left paralyzed from the waist down by gunfire in the 1965 India-Pakistan war. He took up swimming during his recovery and won gold in the 50m freestyle at the 1972 Heidelberg Paralympics, setting a world record - India's first-ever Paralympic gold medal.

Five stories, one pattern: a satellite system built to stop depending on someone else's GPS, a chip industry built to stop depending on imports, a body that found a new way to move when the old one was taken away, careers that turned Indian training into leadership inside the world's top institutions, and a gift aimed squarely at who gets to walk through that door next.
